items.title: Node.js Brotli Decoder Bug Could Allow Remote Code Execution in All Supported Versions
items.summary: Node.js released security updates on Oct 21 for its 22.x, 24.x, and 26.x lines, fixing 10 flaws. The most serious is a Brotli decompression bug that could enable remote code execution on all supported versions.

items.title: Oracle Patches Over 1,200 Vulnerabilities With October 2026 CPU
items.summary: Oracle released patches for more than 1,200 vulnerabilities, including nearly 100 rated critical. The focus was on Fusion Middleware. The update was part of the October 2026 CPU release.

items.title: AI-found bugs are expected to rise, and OpenAI has a five-stage response plan
items.summary: OpenAI announced a five‑stage process to handle critical vulnerabilities in widely used software. The plan evolved after discovering PHP flaws with GPT‑5.6 Sol. It is part of the Patch the Planet initiative.

items.title: Meta Ordered to Pay New Mexico $25 Billion for Deceiving Users About Privacy on Facebook
items.summary: A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for privacy deception on Facebook. The award exceeds the FTC’s $5 billion fine. The case highlights regulatory scrutiny.

items.title: Delinea gives AI assistants read-only access to governance data
items.summary: Delinea introduced Fastpath MCP Server, giving AI assistants read‑only access to access‑governance data. Teams can ask natural‑language questions and receive risk and audit insights. Remediation options are provided in seconds.

items.title: New QPACK Flaws Can Crash HTTP/3 Servers, Trigger Up to 4,000-Fold Memory Amplification
items.summary: FoxIO disclosed QPACK vulnerabilities that let unauthenticated attackers crash HTTP/3 servers. The flaw can trigger up to 4,000‑fold memory amplification with a single crafted header packet. Proof‑of‑concept code was released.

items.title: Certification authority eMudhra defends its laughably weak private keys
items.summary: Certification authority eMudhra defended its private‑key security after audits. The company cited a minor error but faced criticism for weak key management. The issue raised concerns about CA resilience.

items.title: Someone Tried to Exploit PHP2Shell 4 Days Before the Vulnerabilities Were Publicly Disclosed
items.summary: Amazon’s Threat Intelligence team detected an exploit attempt targeting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities on October 17, 2026. The attempt originated from an IP linked to a commercial anonymization network. The flaws were widely exploited after patch release.

items.title: How APT41 revived the BlackLotus bootkit to attack diplomatic organizations in Central Asia
items.summary: Kaspersky identified a new UEFI bootkit, BlackX, used by APT41. The bootkit exploits the Baton Drop vulnerability (CVE‑2022‑21894) and resembles the BlackLotus bootkit. It targets diplomatic organizations in Central Asia.

items.title: Sovereignty vs. security: Microsoft’s Roger Halbheer says you’re asking the wrong question
items.summary: Microsoft’s Roger Halbheer argued that digital sovereignty is a security question first. He highlighted detection speed and cost curves for on‑premises workloads. Boards often seek independence but face steep costs.

items.title: UAE Transitions 50% of Gov't Services to Agentic AI
items.summary: The UAE announced it will transition 50 % of its government services to agentic AI. The move focuses on building a secure and safe foundation for the transformation. It marks a significant shift in public service delivery.

items.title: China-Linked Hackers Use ARTEX AI Agents in ConnectWise Supply Chain Attack
items.summary: Microsoft disclosed that a China state‑aligned actor, Storm‑0940, used the ARTEX AI framework in a supply‑chain attack on ConnectWise Cloud Backup. The attack targeted more than 2,250 tenants with 2,900 sign‑in attempts per minute.

items.summary: PHP remains one of the most widely deployed server-side languages on the web. Estimates suggest it powers close to 70% of all websites, from small personal blogs to large-scale government services, banking platforms,…

items.title: Smashing Security podcast #489: How a brand new crypto wallet came with a spy inside
items.summary: The Smashing Security podcast explores a new hardware crypto wallet that may contain a spy device. It also discusses malicious ads targeting journalists and the use of AI agents on employee laptops.

items.title: PHP blames supply chain security biz Chainguard for putting huge chunks of the web at risk
items.summary: Chainguard CEO criticized coordinated vulnerability disclosure practices, arguing they expose large portions of the web to risk. The company claims its approach is safer for the ecosystem.

items.title: Google Chrome adds Gemini-powered scam detection, warns users of ClickFix attacks
items.summary: Google Chrome now uses Gemini‑powered scam detection to identify deceptive websites and warns users about ClickFix copy‑paste attacks. The feature is part of Chrome’s enhanced protection.

items.title: Microsoft pins ConnectWise supply-chain attack to China-state aligned threat group
items.summary: Microsoft attributes the ConnectWise supply‑chain breach to Storm‑0940, a China‑state aligned group that used an AI penetration testing framework to automate attacks across thousands of tenants.

items.title: Japan's Onamae Desktop Cloud hacked, up to 27,000 servers affected
items.summary: Hackers compromised Onamae Desktop Cloud infrastructure in Japan, installing malware on up to 26,739 customer servers. The breach affected a large number of VPS users.

items.title: TiDB Breach Exposes Flawed Cloud Security Assumptions
items.summary: A breach of TiDB revealed that cloud providers may store sensitive customer data without mutual awareness, exposing data when providers are compromised. The incident highlights flawed security assumptions.

items.title: Russian hackers teamed up to wipe data at Ukrainian grain firm
items.summary: Russian state‑linked group Sandworm collaborated with another threat actor to destroy data at a Ukrainian grain logistics company. The attack was destructive and targeted critical infrastructure.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Asymptote Labs Lands $5.5 Million Seed for AI Agent Runtime Security
items.summary: Asymptote Labs raised $5.5 million in seed funding led by Tower Research Ventures to commercialize its Beacon AI agent runtime security platform. The company aims to secure AI agents in production.

items.title: Google Chrome Adds ClickFix Warnings to Stop Users From Running Malicious Commands
items.summary: Google is rolling out Chrome safeguards to block ClickFix attacks, preventing users from copying and pasting malicious commands. The new feature is available with Enhanced Protection enabled.

items.title: Decades-Old Windows Utility Powers Modern ClickFix Attack
items.summary: The attack uses malicious Google search results related to Amazon and leverages the "finger" utility to launch a CAPTCHA that installs malware, including the Lumma stealer.

items.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously undocumented China-aligned threat cluster known as Bronze Sandcastle that has been observed targeting organizations in Asia and Africa since mid-2025.…

items.title: Ransomware Attacks Rise as Rival Gangs Vie For Market Supremacy
items.summary: Cybercriminal groups The Gentlemen and Qilin dominate ransomware attacks - and both are evolving their tactics in an attempt to outdo one another
